title: Rome's 'Scripture cannot prove Scripture' does not defeat sufficiency
source_text: XX. Atque hinc patet quomodo occurrendum sit argumento, quo se plurimum jactant Pontificii, dum, scilicet, se demonstrare putant Scripturam non esse plenam & sufficientem fidei regulam, quoniam ipsa Scriptura per Scripturam probari non potest. Nec enim, ut patet ex dictis, ad perfectionem & sufficientiam regulae requiritur, ut possit seipsam probare. Sed satis est ut per eam examinari & probari possint omnia praeter ipsam quae sunt ejusdem generis. Ac praeterea in fidei analysi, nisi quis velit admittere circulum, aut progressum in infinitum, quorum utrunque absurdum est, necesse est devenire ad principium quoddam in quo sistendum sit, & quod probari non possit per aliud in eo genere notius, nec etiam seipsum probare, quandoquidem, ut dictum est, nihil probat seipsum.
pass_a_gloss: And from this it is clear how one must meet the argument with which the Pontificals greatly boast, while, namely, they think they demonstrate that Scripture is not a full and sufficient rule of faith, because Scripture itself cannot be proved by Scripture. For neither, as is clear from what has been said, is it required for the perfection and sufficiency of a rule that it be able to prove itself. But it is enough that by it all things besides itself which are of the same kind can be examined and proved. And besides, in the analysis of faith, unless someone wishes to admit a circle, or a progress to infinity, both of which are absurd, it is necessary to come down to some principle in which one must stop, and which cannot be proved by another better known in that kind, nor even prove itself, since, as has been said, nothing proves itself.
pass_b_english: Here is how to meet the argument Rome loves: that Scripture is not a full and sufficient rule of faith because Scripture cannot be proved by Scripture.
A rule need not prove itself to be perfect and sufficient. It is enough that by it everything else of the same kind can be examined and proved.

In analyzing faith, unless you allow a circle or an infinite regress — both absurd — you must stop at some principle that cannot be proved by another better known in that order, and that cannot prove itself. Nothing proves itself.

choices.why: Le Blanc's usual label for Roman controversialists.
Standard scholastic absurdity pair with circulum.
